title: Check: Reactions of Acids with Carbonates

questions.stem: What are the three products when a carbonate reacts with an acid?
questions.explanation: When a carbonate reacts with an acid, three products are formed: a salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas. The CO₂ is observed as fizzing or effervescence. The general equation is: Metal carbonate + Acid → Salt + Water + CO₂.

questions.stem: What is the test for carbon dioxide gas?

options.text: Hold a burning splint and listen for a squeaky pop
Bubble it through limewater; it turns milky
Hold a glowing splint and it relights
Add universal indicator and it turns purple

questions.explanation: The test for carbon dioxide is to bubble the gas through limewater (calcium hydroxide solution). If CO₂ is present, the limewater turns milky or cloudy due to the formation of insoluble calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O.
